observations.statement: This document is an external adapter-mapping guide; A2A is rejected for internal orchestration, and internal retry, resume, child-run control, and lineage remain owned elsewhere.
Persistent storage semantics, tool policy, UI behavior, transport mechanics beyond the bridge surface, and PM-internal orchestration are explicit non-goals.

The mapping is restricted to the existing V0 types `text_delta`, `thinking_delta`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `usage`, `auth_state`, `diagnostic`, `error`, and `done`; payload definitions are delegated to the facade owner.

Provider diagnostics must use reserved categories and the common diagnostic slot; runtime diagnostics require `schema_version`, `run_id`, `source`, and `attempt_id`, while pre-admission diagnostics use `pre_attempt`.
The common diagnostic slot separates PM runtime `attempt_id` from upstream provider/session/task identity and forbids compatibility tier labels from becoming runtime routing keys.
Native mappings cover text, tool calls/results, usage, terminal completion, HITL, errors, handoffs, and raw observations, including legacy-call preference and correlation fallback behavior.
A2A AgentCard data is capability evidence only, terminal upstream Tasks are immutable, A2A transports remain provider variants, and cross-task prompt-cache continuity cannot be assumed.
A2A mappings cover submitted, working, input-required, completed, messages, text/data parts, artifacts, streaming updates, task statuses, remote responses, and agent wrappers.
Missing tool IDs use `pm-synth-{run_id}-{seq}`, and upstream UUID deduplication uses a 10000-entry LRU seen-set.
Input-required is a paused, non-terminal state; context IDs are upstream A2A context IDs or deterministic native IDs, sequence continuity is preserved, and matching input resumes emission.
An authentication barrier requires an `auth_state` event, while prompts, device flows, and key refresh remain exclusively owned by the auth subsystem.

Binary artifacts must be persisted rather than streamed, artifact updates carry identity and chunk metadata, successful file persistence emits `artifact_file_part`, and raw observations use a 500-entry ring with a 4 KiB truncation threshold.
Tool correlation requires one result per use, placeholder uses for orphan results, synthetic missing results before `done`, and raw-observation preservation of extra results.
The terminal invariant requires exactly one final `done`, prefers RunCompletion semantics, and converts additional terminal indicators to raw observations.
The Overseer instrumentation specifies tier-boundary audits, exactly two reviewers, a three-way consensus matrix, an override flag, and reconstruction from diagnostic events alone.
The continuity addenda require retry/remediation lineage, deterministic blocked-flow wakes, canonical wake reasons, and separation of runtime attempt identity from provider continuity.
Acceptance carry-through requires provider-native placement of OpenCode/A2A session identifiers and an `approval_scope_key` spanning actor, lane, run, and account context across four consumers.
The stated continuity acceptance criteria are preservation of retry/remediation lineage and deterministic waking from input-provided or resume events.

candidate_findings.summary: External-only authority conflicts with normative Overseer execution
candidate_findings.obligation: Keep this owner external-bridge-only and leave PM-internal orchestration, child-run control, and scheduling to the declared runtime owners.
candidate_findings.gap: The normative audit section states that the Overseer performs tier audits and spawns exactly two reviewer subagents without saying whether the bridge merely observes those actions or enforces them, conflicting with the document's declared authority boundary.

candidate_findings.summary: Termination outcome classification has no deterministic rule
candidate_findings.obligation: Derive `run_finished.outcome` and `done.status` deterministically from every `TerminationEvent.termination_reason`.
candidate_findings.gap: The mapping delegates success-versus-failure to unspecified reason analysis and provides no reason table, predicate, fallback, or unknown-reason behavior.

candidate_findings.summary: Terminal preference lacks an online arbitration boundary
candidate_findings.obligation: Emit exactly one final `done` while preferring RunCompletion semantics whenever they are available.
candidate_findings.gap: No buffering window, end-of-input signal, or finality rule defines how an adapter receiving `TerminationEvent` first can know whether a later `RunCompletionEvent` will become available; suppression of a second `run_finished` is also not stated explicitly.

candidate_findings.summary: Fatal versus near-fatal ErrorEvent behavior is unresolved
candidate_findings.obligation: Map upstream errors while preserving the distinction between continuing errors and errors that terminate with a final `done`.
candidate_findings.gap: `error` is described as fatal or near-fatal, but every `ErrorEvent` receives the same category and message mapping with no fatality discriminator, continuation rule, terminal status, or required `done` behavior.

candidate_findings.summary: Native run-start emission has no trigger or ordering rule
candidate_findings.obligation: Emit `run_started` exactly once when a native adapter begins processing a provider run.
candidate_findings.gap: The reserved category defines this obligation, but the exhaustive native mapping table assigns no native event or adapter lifecycle action to `run_started`; only the A2A submitted state has an explicit trigger.

candidate_findings.summary: A2A non-success terminal states are not mapped exactly
candidate_findings.obligation: Map every A2A task state transition to an exact step diagnostic and map every terminal state to an exact `done` status and outcome.
candidate_findings.gap: Only `TaskState.completed` has an explicit success mapping; the generic TaskStatus row says step-started or step-finished and says terminal states trigger `done` without enumerating state-to-category selection, failure states, cancellation states, outcomes, or statuses.

candidate_findings.summary: A2A message role and resume eligibility are underspecified
candidate_findings.obligation: Classify A2A message roles deterministically and emit `input_provided` only as a correlated resume using the paused context ID.
candidate_findings.gap: The mapping uses undefined user-equivalent and assistant-equivalent classifications and does not state whether every user-equivalent message is a resume or only one received while paused, although the pause contract requires the same context ID.

candidate_findings.summary: Artifact streaming conflicts with DataPart non-text handling
candidate_findings.obligation: Prevent non-text or binary DataPart content from entering `text_delta` while allowing text projections only when they exist.
candidate_findings.gap: The DataPart row makes text projection conditional and forbids non-text in `text_delta`, while the streaming-update row says each part becomes a StreamEvent and each maps to `text_delta`; no precedence or part filter resolves the two rules.

candidate_findings.summary: Artifact persistence failure has no normalized failure path
candidate_findings.obligation: Persist every binary artifact and emit a file-part diagnostic only after successful persistence.
candidate_findings.gap: The specification defines only the successful `persisted=true` path and does not define the event, error status, retry behavior, artifact reference behavior, or run outcome when required persistence fails.

candidate_findings.summary: Auth-barrier classification is delegated without an adapter mapping
candidate_findings.obligation: Detect every supported authentication barrier and choose the correct canonical `auth_state.payload.state` without attempting autonomous recovery.
candidate_findings.gap: Barrier detection and state selection are expressed through examples and an appropriate external state value; the capsule provides no exhaustive transport-condition mapping, fallback, or behavior for an unrecognized authentication barrier.

candidate_findings.summary: Final audit verdict computation is not defined
candidate_findings.obligation: Emit a reconstructable final verdict from reviewer consensus, verifier result, and any legitimate forced-remediation decision.
candidate_findings.gap: Consensus values are deterministic, but `final_verdict` has no allowed-value set or transition table, escalation has no disposition, and the discretionary override has no authority predicate or rule for setting `forced_remediation`.

candidate_findings.summary: Retry addendum uses conflicting unqualified attempt identity
candidate_findings.obligation: Keep runtime dispatch identity distinct from upstream provider continuity across reconnects, retries, resumes, and remediation reruns.
candidate_findings.gap: One addendum says resumed or retried runs preserve attempt identity when upstream exposes it, while the versioned rules say retries and prerequisite resumes always create a new runtime `attempt_id` and preserve upstream continuity in `provider_attempt_ref?`; the earlier unqualified term is not reconciled.

candidate_findings.summary: Wake reasons have neither a normalized location nor deterministic classifiers
candidate_findings.obligation: Preserve each canonical wake reason in the normalized stream and select the exact reason for each triggering event.
candidate_findings.gap: The diagnostic slot description does not locate `wake_reason`; the wake table does not name an event type or category that carries it, and completion plus approval/input resolution use alternatives without defining the applicable classifier.

candidate_findings.summary: The required canonical data shape is absent and session routing is ambiguous
candidate_findings.obligation: Define the exact fields that store OpenCode/A2A session identifiers without replacing canonical runtime identity.
candidate_findings.gap: The core ends immediately after the Required data shape heading; context gives prose constraints but does not decide whether a session identifier belongs in `correlation_id?`, `provider_attempt_ref?`, both, or another bridge-only field, nor does it provide types or cardinality.

candidate_findings.summary: Approval Scope Key lacks a canonical contract
candidate_findings.obligation: Define and reuse one approval scope key across actor, lane, run, account, permissions, HITL, doom-loop protection, and session approval caching.
candidate_findings.gap: The acceptance bullets name dimensions and consumers but provide no field location, component ordering, canonical serialization, nullability, equality semantics, lifecycle, invalidation rule, or collision behavior.

candidate_findings.summary: Continuity acceptance has no executable evidence contract
candidate_findings.obligation: Demonstrate that normalization preserves retry/remediation lineage and deterministically wakes blocked flows.
candidate_findings.gap: The acceptance criteria are outcome statements only; no event trace, fixture, assertion, required receipt, failure case, or pass/fail procedure is identified.

candidate_findings.summary: Legacy and modern logical-call deduplication has no identity rule
candidate_findings.obligation: Prefer ToolCallEvent over FunctionCallEvent when both represent the same logical call and avoid double-emitting a tool lifecycle.
candidate_findings.gap: The native mapping invokes sameness of a logical call but defines no correlation key, ordering window, buffering rule, or fallback by which an adapter can determine that the two event forms are duplicates.

candidate_findings.summary: Malformed tool-argument handling is unspecified
candidate_findings.obligation: Convert function argument strings into normalized `payload.arguments` or emit deterministic failure evidence when parsing fails.
candidate_findings.gap: Both tool-call paths require parsed arguments but define no parse format, invalid-input diagnostic, fallback payload, error event, or effect on tool execution.

candidate_findings.summary: Multi-call synthesized ID sequencing is not explicit
candidate_findings.obligation: Give every entry in a multi-entry ToolCallEvent a distinct deterministic `tool_use_id`.
candidate_findings.gap: The event emits one `tool_use` per entry, while synthesis uses the current sequence number; no rule states when sequence advances across entries in the same upstream event, leaving collision avoidance dependent on builder interpretation.

candidate_findings.summary: Optional DataPart text projection creates observable adapter variance
candidate_findings.obligation: Produce a consistent normalized user-visible stream for the same DataPart payload while retaining the full data.
candidate_findings.gap: A text projection MAY be emitted, with no policy deciding when it is emitted; conforming adapters can therefore produce different `text_delta` streams for identical input.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Absence of GUI behavior is intentional because UI/UX and widget rendering are explicit non-goals.
The bridge is explicitly forbidden from introducing new V0 event types.
Diagnostic category namespacing and common runtime identity fields are explicitly constrained.
AgentCard authority, terminal Task immutability, transport status, and cross-task cache assumptions are explicitly bounded.
UUID deduplication capacity, key, eviction policy, duplicate disposition, and optional diagnostic are explicitly stated.
Native and A2A input-required behavior explicitly preserves pause state, context correlation, sequence continuity, and the absence of terminal `done`.
Tool-correlation obligations explicitly cover orphan results, missing results at completion, and repeated results.
The normalized stream has an explicit exactly-one-final-`done` invariant and a stated terminal-source preference.
The two-reviewer consensus matrix is exact for accept, remediate, and disagreement outcomes.
The later identity rules explicitly separate retry-created runtime attempts, provider references, and same-attempt reconnect observation.
Autonomous adapter re-authentication is explicitly prohibited and recovery authority is assigned to the auth subsystem.
Binary content exclusion and successful artifact-persistence reporting are explicit.
